name: Plastipak Packaging Inc
old_description: One of those innovations was the creation of Plastipak—founded in 1967 to solve the problem of the heavy five-gallon jugs used to deliver water. With a full load of water in them, these five-gallon jugs weighed 50 pounds and required superior strength to manage. Plastic seemed the ideal solution to lighten the load, as did manufacturing the plastic in-house. The success of the lightened bottle was the start of Plastipak’s ongoing innovation and success.
about:
Plastipak Packaging Inc. was founded in 1967 in Champaign, Illinois, by Bill Young, who joined his family's water delivery business after graduating from the University of Detroit. The company began as an in-house solution to the heavy five-gallon glass jugs used for water delivery, replacing them with lighter, stronger plastic containers manufactured on site. The Young family has retained ownership through successive generations, embedding a heritage of hands-on innovation into the company's culture.

Today Plastipak operates as a global manufacturer of rigid plastic packaging and recycling solutions, with more than 50 production sites across North America, South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia. Its core processes include extrusion blow molding, injection stretch blow molding (ISBM), PET and ePET molding, wide-mouth container technology, hot-fill and barrier container engineering, decoration (embossing, debossing, direct-object printing), and the production of both virgin and post-consumer recycled (PCR) resins. The company holds over 500 U.S. patents and more than 1,000 international patents, reflecting a portfolio of proprietary systems such as the rotary dual-cavity ISBM machine, the 30-station G.E.M. PAK extrusion wheel, and recent innovations like SprayPET Revolution™ aerosol packaging, PPK Natura™ carbon-waste PET resin, and O2blox™ nylon-free oxygen barrier.

Plastipak serves a broad range of end markets, including carbonated and non-carbonated beverages, hot-fill juices and teas, beer, UHT milk, dairy, household and commercial products (detergents, personal care), automotive, industrial, and agricultural chemicals. Long-standing customers have included Pepsi, Kraft, Heineken, Downy Unstopables, and Hilltop Honey, illustrating the company's reach across multinational brands and regional producers alike.

The business was created to solve a specific logistics problem—reducing the weight and breakage of water delivery jugs—and that problem-solving mindset remains central. Plastipak differentiates itself through vertical integration (in-house resin production, mold design, recycling via its Clean Tech centers), a global footprint that enables local service, and a sustained investment in circular-economy technologies that turn post-consumer waste into new packaging.
